tokyo_shanti_soup_curry_shibuy.price_note: PARTIAL FOR ONE REASON, STATED BY THE SHOP ITSELF: the food page carries 「※各店舗によって取り扱いメニュー、値段が異なりますので、お店備え付けのメニューにてご確認ください」 — menu and prices differ by branch, check the card in the shop. What is below is SHANTi's own chain-wide card, which is the best first-party source that exists for Shibuya; the Shibuya page itself publishes only the address 渋谷区道玄坂2-7-4 and hours 11:00-23:30 (L.O. 23:00), open year-round, with no prices. Treat every number as the chain's, not as a Shibuya guarantee. ⚠ THE REASON THIS RECORD MATTERS TO A COELIAC IS THAT SOUP CURRY IS THE ONE JAPANESE CURRY FORM THAT IS NOT THICKENED WITH A WHEAT ROUX. Japanese curry rice is built on a flour-and-fat roux and is a flat no; Sapporo-style soup curry is a thin spiced broth over rice, and SHANTi says its original soup is 20種類以上のスパイス with no thickener mentioned. That makes this one of the more promising forms in the whole dataset — and it is still recorded as ask, not gf, because the shop publishes NO allergen sheet and does not say what its stock is made from. This is the difference between a dish that is worth asking about and a dish that has been cleared. Ask about the soup base and the fried toppings, which share a fryer. ⚠ THE TOPPING LIST IS WHERE THE WHEAT ACTUALLY IS, AND IT IS EASY TO MISS: MOMO is described by the shop as 水餃子, a boiled dumpling — a wheat wrapper sold as a Nepalese speciality; ハンバーグ, コロッケ, シッディ春巻 and パスケ (a ベーコンとチーズ入りの餃子) are all wheat; 揚げ物 toppings (揚げ茄子, 揚げかぼちゃ, 揚げたまねぎ, 揚げブロッコリー, 揚げ餅, 唐揚げ) are fried and 唐揚げ is wheat-dredged, so the oil is shared. ⚠ AND ONE GENUINELY USEFUL VEGAN FINDING: ベジタブルスープカレー at 1,300円 is a permanent vegetable-only bowl and 揚げ茄子/スイートコーン/揚げかぼちゃ/パプリカ are plant toppings — but the stock is undeclared and soup curry stocks are conventionally chicken, so it is recorded vegan: ask, not vegan. The shop notes MOMO contains no garlic (にんにくは入ってません), which tells you they field ingredient questions. The heat scale runs 40+ steps from 弱辛 to 超汁男 with surcharges from +50円 at level 5 up to +550円 at level 50.

tokyo_shabu_shabu_retasu_shibu.price_note: ⚠ READ THIS BEFORE USING ANY LUNCH PRICE YOU FIND FOR THIS SHOP, INCLUDING ELSEWHERE IN THIS DATASET. The chain's own lunch page opens with 「渋谷店のみ、ランチタイムは下記メニューではなく、食べ放題メニューを実施しております」 — SHIBUYA ALONE does not serve the printed lunch card at all; it runs an all-you-can-eat lunch instead, and the operator does not publish what that costs. The single-serving lunch prices on that page (1,000-1,800円 by broth and meat) belong to the other branches and are deliberately NOT recorded here, because attaching them to Shibuya would be wrong. The site adds the usual 「金額やメニューは各店舗で異なる場合がございます」 over everything. What is recorded below is the chain's course card and drink list, which is the best first-party source for Shibuya; the branch page itself gives only 渋谷区宇田川町28-2 ニュー渋谷ビル2階, 12:00-22:00 (L.O. 21:30, last entry 21:00), 50 seats, closed only over new year. ⚠ THE FORMAT IS THE POINT AND IT IS UNUSUALLY GOOD NEWS FOR A COELIAC: 一人一鍋, one pot per person. Shabu-shabu is already among the safer Japanese forms — meat and vegetables swished in broth, no batter, no noodle — and an individual pot removes the shared-broth cross-contact that makes communal nabe a problem. That is a real structural advantage and it is why this record is worth having. ⚠ BUT THE RISK MOVES TO THE BROTH, THE DIP AND THE 〆, AND ALL THREE ARE WHEAT ROUTES. Of the eight broths, 特選すき焼き is made with 但馬の地醤油 こむらさき — declared soy sauce, so a flat no. 胡麻坦々だし is sold on 〆には極上担々麺, a wheat noodle finisher, and 韓国辛ジャンスープ uses コチュジャン and 豆板醤, both conventionally wheat-fermented. The dips are worse than the broths: 生搾りぽん酢 and 塩レモンぽん酢 are ponzu, i.e. soy plus citrus. ⚠ WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH ASKING FOR: the 匠の昆布だし is kombu and green tea, and クリーミー豆乳だし is soy milk — both plant-based and neither contains declared wheat, and the ブレンド塩胡椒 and にんにくオイル dips are salt-pepper and garlic oil rather than soy. A kombu or soy-milk pot with the salt-pepper dip is the order to build here, and 豆乳だし with vegetables is the nearest thing to a vegan meal, though the shop does not say whether the soy-milk broth is dashi-fortified. Recorded ask throughout: the shop publishes no allergen sheet. ⚠ ONE ODD DISCLOSURE THE SHOP MAKES ITSELF, worth repeating because it is unusual honesty: the course page warns 「とんタンは肉の整形の為に食用結着剤を使用しているものがございます」 — the pork tongue may be reformed using a food-grade binding agent. Binding agents are often transglutaminase preparations, which are frequently carried on a wheat or dairy substrate.

tokyo_choraku_dogenzaka_ten.price_note: NO MENU EXISTS TO FIND AT THIS ADDRESS AND THAT IS THE FINDING. choraku.tokyo — the URL this dataset carries as 兆楽's website — resolves to 渋谷兆楽's Shopify MERCHANDISE STORE, not to a restaurant site. Its entire catalogue is four items: CHORAKU IN THE HOOD TEE (¥8,800, sold out), FRIED RICE PRINT PLATE (¥6,600), CHORAKU DRAGON TEE (¥5,500) and CHORAKU STAFF TEE (¥5,500), plus a banner for a BLACK EYE PATCH × 兆楽 tee drop. The site's only other pages are /cart and the three Shopify policy pages; there is no food navigation, no 品書き, no branch list and no address block anywhere on it. ⚠ THE PRICES ON THAT SITE ARE T-SHIRTS AND A PLATE, AND ANY PASS THAT SCRAPES ¥ FIGURES OFF IT WILL PRODUCE AN 8,800円 'MENU ITEM' FOR A RAMEN SHOP — the ¥6,600 line is literally a printed dish with a fried-rice design on it, which is exactly the sort of thing that reads as food to a machine. This record is recorded EMPTY on purpose so that it is not selected again. The shop's food menu is not published on any first-party page reachable from this URL; the only remaining route is its Tabelog 品書き, which is parked while Tabelog serves a Cloudflare managed challenge to this egress.

tokyo_matcha_times_asakusa.price_note: PARTIAL FOR TWO SEPARATE REASONS, AND BOTH SHOULD BE READ BEFORE THE LIST. First, the site publishes ITS MENU WITHOUT A SINGLE PRICE — every drink and sweet below carries a one-line tasting description from the brand and no figure at all, so nothing here is priced and nothing has been invented. Second, and more important for this record: MATCHA-TIMES.COM IS A BRAND SITE, NOT THIS SHOP'S SITE. It belongs to 株式会社MATCHA TIMES of 東京都中野区本町2-4-11, a company its own About page says was formed in 2025 by people who had been promoting matcha abroad, and the site's navigation is ホーム / MATCHA TIMESについて / メニュー / ギャラリー / FC加盟 / お問合せ — a franchise-recruitment structure. IT CARRIES NO BRANCH LIST AND THE WORD 浅草 APPEARS NOWHERE ON ANY PAGE OF IT. The menu below is therefore the brand's menu, which is the best first-party evidence available for the Asakusa shop, but it has not been confirmed against that branch and a franchised outlet may not carry every line. The company states it buys its matcha powder from five long-established matcha houses. ⚠ THE DIET SHAPE OF A MATCHA CAFÉ IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. Matcha itself is a ground leaf — no wheat, no animal — so the tea is never the problem; the problem is always what it is served in or with. Every ラテ on this list is milk, which makes the entire drinks column non-vegan except the two that are not lattes. And the sweets column splits cleanly on batter: たいやき, どら焼き, ロールケーキ and クッキー are wheat by construction, while 大福, ようかん and わらび餅 are rice, agar and starch confections that are the genuine leads here. ⚠ ONE ITEM IS A REAL TRAP: 抹茶ソフトクリーム is dairy AND normally arrives in a wheat cone, so it fails both diets at once in a shop where almost everything else fails only one.

tokyo_chouchou_shizenha_wine_t.price_note: PARTIAL BECAUSE THE SHOP DOES NOT PUBLISH PRICES, NOT BECAUSE THE SOURCE IS WEAK. chouchou-nature.com is the bistro's own site and it is unusually forthcoming about WHAT it cooks and completely silent about what anything costs: the menu section is organised as four seasonal blocks — spring, summer, autumn, winter — each with a paragraph on the season's character followed by a list of that season's dishes, and not one figure appears anywhere on the page. Every dish below is named by the shop; none is priced and none has been guessed. ⚠ THE DISHES ROTATE BY SEASON, SO THE LIST IS NOT A BOARD YOU CAN ORDER FROM ON ANY GIVEN DAY — a winter cassoulet and a spring white-asparagus dish never coexist. The season is recorded in each note. Owner-chef 片野裕介 opened it in Shibuya in 2016 after AU COCHON ROSE, R&D, ポンレヴェック and スペインバル ジローナ. 〒150-0031 東京都渋谷区桜丘町30-10 青野ビル1F, tel/fax 03-6416-3868. ⚠ THE WINE ANSWER IS THAT THERE IS NO WINE LIST, AND THAT IS THE SHOP'S POLICY RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: it states plainly that natural wine is made in small quantities so it cannot keep a fixed stock, and that staff will choose a bottle to taste and budget instead. For a vegan that matters — VIN NATUREL IS THE ONE CATEGORY OF WINE MOST LIKELY TO BE UNFINED AND UNFILTERED, so this is a room where the question can actually be answered by the person pouring, but it cannot be answered from the website. ⚠ AND THE BREAD IS THE OTHER HEADLINE: the shop bakes its own, keeps about seven of the thirteen named loaves on any day, and the list contains gorgonzola, cream, milk butter and bacon breads alongside plain ones. All of it is wheat or rye; none of it is a gluten-free option.

That makes the vegan question answerable at the table and unanswerable from the website: natural wine is the category most likely to be unfined and unfiltered, but nothing here confirms any given bottle. The owner names Benoît Rosenberger, lucky13 and loup des vigne as the wines that started him on it.

tokyo_iwao.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE SHOP'S SITE IS A LANDING PAGE, NOT A MENU. asia-kitchen.co.jp/iwao/ has four nav items — HOME, GOOGLE MAP, OFFICIAL and 食べログ — and no menu page behind any of them; the body is a description of the room (a fifty-year-old detached wooden house down a back alley, converted, entered through a small くぐり戸), an empty Instagram feed widget reading 「投稿はありません」, an access block and a list of sister shops (氣ウラ, ウダガワ成ル, ミヤシタ成ル). No dish is named anywhere on it. ⚠ THE PAGE DOES CHARACTERISE THE COOKING AND THAT IS ALL IT DOES: 和食ベースの創作料理 built on 厳選された鮮魚, with a deep shochu and wine list — a creative-Japanese izakaya on selected fresh fish. That is not a menu and nothing has been extracted from it. ⚠ ONE INCONSISTENCY WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN TIDYING: the same page describes the building as 築50年 in one paragraph and 築70年 in another. The only published board is behind the page's own 食べログ link, and Tabelog has served this egress a Cloudflare managed challenge since 2026-09-02, so it is parked rather than missing. 〒150-0043 東京都渋谷区道玄坂2-23-2 巖ビル1・2F, tel 050-5303-3146, 17:30–00:00, irregular closing.

tokyo_ramen_makotoya_shibuya_c.price_note: The branch's own official page publishes the full board with a description and a tax-EXCLUDED price on every line; the 税別 marker is on each figure and is carried through below rather than silently converted. The chain runs about 100 shops from a Kansai base and boils beef bone (5kg per bone, 30kg per batch) in large pressure stockpots at each shop for its 牛骨白湯. Five minutes' walk from Shibuya station, near the Dogenzaka-shita crossing opposite the former Tokyu Honten site. ⚠ ONE WHOLE SOUP BASE IS NOT SOLD AT THIS BRANCH AND THE MENU SAYS SO IN A FOOTNOTE THAT IS EASY TO MISS: 「※伏見稲荷OICYビレッジ店、渋谷センター街本店は鶏じゃんラーメンは販売しておりません」 — THE 鶏じゃん BOWLS ARE NOT AVAILABLE HERE. They are recorded below because they are on the branch's own menu page, each flagged as unavailable at this shop, so that the record does not silently drop five priced lines and so that nobody arrives expecting them. ⚠ THE ITEM THAT WILL FOOL PEOPLE IS THE 糖質オフ麺, AND IT IS WORTH READING THE SHOP'S OWN SENTENCE TWICE: 「糖質ゼロの澱粉を従来の小麦粉と合わせて美味しい麺にできています」 — the zero-carb starch is COMBINED WITH conventional WHEAT FLOUR. A '50% carb-off' noodle at +90円 sounds like the dietary option on the board and IS STILL A WHEAT NOODLE; the shop also notes the figure is for the noodle alone and excludes soup and toppings, and that a 替玉 of it is 250円. ⚠ EVERYTHING ELSE IS AS EXPECTED AND NONE OF IT IS SAFE: ramen noodles are wheat and かん水, the 背脂醤油 base is 熟成醤油 (soy, so wheat) on a 22-gauge Hakata-style thin noodle, chashu is soy-braised, ajitama is marinated in the chashu liquid, gyoza and kara-age are wheat by construction, and the two broths are beef bone and chicken. THERE IS NO VEGAN ROUTE AT ALL — even the free 辛子高菜 on the counter is a pickled mustard green normally seasoned with soy and often dashi.

⚠ THE MOST MISLEADING LINE ON THIS BOARD. It advertises 50% less carbohydrate and the shop's own explanation is that a zero-carbohydrate starch is COMBINED WITH CONVENTIONAL WHEAT FLOUR to make it — so it is a wheat noodle with less starch, not a wheat-free noodle, and it is the only thing on the menu a coeliac might mistake for an accommodation. tokyo_izumo_asakusa_yokocho.price_note: Asakusa Yokocho's own shop page for stall 06 publishes a full priced 主なフードメニュー and 主なドリンクメニュー, all marked 税込, so these are the real counter prices. NOTE ON IDENTITY: this dataset carries the shop under a long compound name (うなぎの蒲の穂焼 牛タン 焼鳥 馬刺し いづも); the venue's own page calls stall 06 「鰻串 いづも」 and lists only the eel-skewer range. The 牛タン/焼鳥/馬刺し in our name belong to OTHER stalls in the same yokocho — Asakusa Yokocho is a shared food alley of eight stalls under one roof, and shops01–shops08 are separate kitchens. Do not attribute a beef-tongue or horse-sashimi dish to this record. ⚠ THE GLUTEN FACT THAT GOVERNS THIS WHOLE MENU IS 蒲焼 TARE. 蒲の穂焼き is a kabayaki preparation: the eel is repeatedly basted with a soy-sauce-and-mirin tare over charcoal, and Japanese soy sauce is a wheat product. The tare pot is shared and the grill bars are shared, so even a skewer ordered plain passes over the same charcoal as basted ones. That is why nothing here is recorded as gf. The shop publishes no allergen sheet.

items.note: ⚠ Kabayaki tare is soy-sauce based, so wheat. The shop's signature and the reason for its name.
⚠ An assortment built from the tare-basted range above.
The page does not say whether this cut is tare-basted or salted. Shared charcoal grill with kabayaki either way — ask.
白 normally marks the shioyaki version, i.e. no tare — but the shop does not say so, and the grill is shared. Ask before assuming.
